messages:
sara: infra-alert: multiple flashpack-2 nodes in eu-south2 reporting nvme temp throttle and io drop, seeing attach queue backlog for gpu pods. dashboard https://dash.redwood.internal/cluster/eu-south2 :warning:
ops-bot: ALERT nvme_temp_high cluster=eu-south2 nodes=53 peak_temp=86C iops_drop=35%
luca: noticed firmware 1.3.7 rolled last night to flashpack-2 fleet (batch B). correlation looks strong on batch ids. logs show `nvme0 timeout` and ECC counters rising.
rahul: ops telemetry shows rack row3 AC hiccup at 02:10 UTC too. could be environmental + fw combo.
sara: plan suggestion: 1) cordon affected nodes (start with 15) 2) pause janitor/scrub on those nodes 3) spin up temporary capacity in eu-west1 to keep critical queues healthy 4) collect SMART and dmesg and open vendor ticket.
luca: agree. we should avoid mass drains because Dedicated customers can't tolerate long reschedules. suggest progressive drains with priority for preemptible/gpu-burst jobs first.
rahul: I've created OP-5389 for on-site AC tech, ETA ~40m. also enabling emergency fan profile on row3 PDUs.
infra-bot: OP-5389 created and associated with INC-2026-348. contact vendor: nvme-vendor-support@parts.example, severity=high.
sara: cost note: temporarily auto-scaling eu-west1 100 vGPUs for 12h estimates ~\$3.6k. ok to approve for customer-facing SLO?
luca: yes for now. prioritize customer-facing pools.
rahul: starting cordon+drain script on first 15 nodes: `./tools/cordon_and_drain.sh --nodes-file nodes_eus2_thermal_batch1.txt --batch-size 5`
sara: collectors: `nvme smart-log` and `journalctl -k` on sample nodes, upload to inc page. avoid reboot unless vendor asks.
infra-bot: collecting SMART logs: job 9876 queued.
luca: if vendor confirms fw regression we need rollback plan. rollback risk: write path differences could cause small window of additional io. prepare comms for Dedicated customers.
rahul: vendor call scheduled in 25m. will share call notes here.
sara: thanks. keeping infra-oncall and eng-ops in loop. updating incident INC-2026-348 doc now.
